name: Natural World Image Collections Benchmark
description: Recent progress in self-supervised learning has resulted in models that are capable of extracting rich representations from image collections without requiring any explicit label supervision. However, to date the vast majority of these approaches have restricted themselves to training on standard benchmark datasets such as ImageNet. We argue that fine-grained visual categorization problems, such as plant and animal species classification, provide an informative testbed for self-supervised learning. In order to facilitate progress in this area we present two new natural world visual classification datasets, iNat2021 and NeWT. The former consists of 2.7M images from 10k different species uploaded by users of the citizen science application iNaturalist. We designed the latter, NeWT, in collaboration with domain experts with the aim of benchmarking the performance of representation learning algorithms on a suite of challenging natural world binary classification tasks that go beyond standard species classification. These two new datasets allow us to explore questions related to large-scale representation and transfer learning in the context of fine-grained categories. We provide a comprehensive analysis of feature extractors trained with and without supervision on ImageNet and iNat2021, shedding light on the strengths and weaknesses of different learned features across a diverse set of tasks. We find that features produced by standard supervised methods still outperform those produced by self-supervised approaches such as SimCLR. However, improved self-supervised learning methods are constantly being released and the iNat2021 and NeWT datasets are a valuable resource for tracking their progress.
evaluation_method: top-1 accuracy (and transfer/linear-probing accuracy for representation evaluation)
typical_sota_score: around 70–90% top-1 on iNat2021 depending on model size and training; NeWT binary tasks vary more and are typically lower
reputation: iNat2021 and NeWT are well-regarded resources in fine-grained/ecology vision research and are commonly used to evaluate representation learning and transfer performance.
notes: Large-scale, long-tailed, and noisy real-world image collections (class imbalance and label noise); non-LLM benchmark; transfer/representation metrics matter as much as direct classification scores.
